rules.source: Android uiautomator dump (AccessibilityNodeInfo.getClassName/getText/getContentDescription/getBoundsInScreen)
rules.rationale: The adapter creates exactly one graph node per <node> element of the dump (plus the Document node); the containment tree is the node's `parent`. Container roots (<hierarchy>, <AppiumAUT>) are not nodes.

rules.source: Android uiautomator dump (AccessibilityNodeInfo.getClassName/getText/getContentDescription/getBoundsInScreen)
rules.rationale: Records on the Document node that the facts came from an Android view-hierarchy dump (static; one moment of one screen).

rules.source: Android AccessibilityNodeInfo getClassName() mapped by Ozone's class-suffix table (AppCompat/Material subclasses end with the framework widget name)
rules.rationale: Class suffix [class$="Layout"],[class$="ViewGroup"] => role 'group'. Generic suffixes run in phase 1 and specific ones in phase 2, so the more specific widget wins.

rules.source: android.webkit.WebView
rules.rationale: A WebView renders a web page: its content is NOT in this dump. The node is a boundary; the page behind it is analyzed with the html / dom-live flavors and linked.

rules.source: Android uiautomator dump (AccessibilityNodeInfo.getClassName/getText/getContentDescription/getBoundsInScreen)
rules.rationale: Last resort: the tail of resource-id (com.app:id/login_btn => login_btn). A developer-chosen identifier, not user-facing text.

rules.source: AccessibilityNodeInfo.getHintText
rules.rationale: An empty EditText exposes its hint as the visible prompt.

rules.source: AccessibilityNodeInfo.getText
rules.rationale: Visible text is the accessible name when there is no content description. Password fields never reach this rule: their text is dropped at parse time.

rules.source: AccessibilityNodeInfo.getContentDescription
rules.rationale: An explicit content description is the author's accessible name and wins over visible text.

rules.rationale: Password fields never have their text emitted: the parser drops it before the graph is built, and this flag says so.

rules.source: Prompt-injection indicators
rules.rationale: Flags (never removes) screen text that addresses an AI reader or tries to override its instructions. All screen text is untrusted display data.
evidence: text / content-desc / hint matched a known injection pattern

rules.source: AccessibilityNodeInfo.isVisibleToUser
rules.rationale: The node is not visible to the user according to the platform (scrolled off, covered or invisible).

rules.source: Android AccessibilityNodeInfo isClickable/isLongClickable/isCheckable
rules.rationale: Nodes that accept a tap, long-press or toggle.

rules.source: Android AccessibilityNodeInfo isFocusable
rules.rationale: Focusable nodes accept keyboard/D-pad focus; enabled state is applied in the final rule.

rules.source: AccessibilityNodeInfo.isVisibleToUser
rules.rationale: A not-visible node hides its subtree for reading and acting.

rules.source: Ozone
rules.rationale: interactable = (clickable || long-clickable || checkable || focusable) && enabled && effectively visible.
